title: Four MD5 blocks in the printed LP2-56 target
question: Does any preserved puzzle artifact's exact MD5 digest equal a complete 16-byte block of the printed 64-byte LP2-56 target?
reader_question: Could the LP2-56 number be four MD5 hashes?
summary: Splits the printed LP2-56 64-byte value into four aligned 16-byte blocks and compares each with MD5 of the fixed preserved-artifact corpus.
finding: None of the four printed 16-byte blocks matches MD5 of any of 324 distinct candidate byte strings. One digest per unique input, compared with four blocks, gives 1,296 exact comparisons; 412 names include aliases of identical bytes. First- and last-block planted controls passed, as did the independent recount.
limitations: Only this exact byte-zero block partition, MD5 and the frozen preserved-artifact corpus were tested. It does not evaluate the unknown web page, arbitrary new inputs, modified bytes, other digests, offsets or encodings. No historical MD5-block claim is attributed or replayed.
next_steps: Any narrower four-MD5 proposal should specify four input byte strings and their order before checking the target; an unknown-page hunt needs a justified candidate source and finite search bound.

scope.representation: The archived LP2-56 reading's 128 hexadecimal characters decoded as 64 bytes, divided into four consecutive complete 16-byte blocks; the same 412 named artifact variants and 324 unique byte strings as the frozen earlier corpus.
scope.procedure: Verify printed target and source-file hashes; compute MD5 once for each unique candidate byte string; compare all 16 bytes at each of four fixed block positions; independently reconstruct inputs and check planted controls.
scope.parameters: Four byte-zero-aligned 16-byte target blocks; MD5 only; 324 × 4 = 1,296 exact comparisons. Known MD5('abc') vector and first/last synthetic block controls.
scope.exclusions: Unknown web pages or other corpus inputs, byte permutations, encodings beyond the frozen variants, truncated or reversed digests, offsets, alternative hash algorithms and hypotheses about the four-part message.

review.reviewer: Independent source-byte reconstruction and four-block MD5 checker

reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library; run from the Liberpedia checkout with pinned images and page data.
